title: EDGAR Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) - SEC, Last Reviewed or Updated: April 8, 2025
source_kind: SEC's own documentation page for the data.sec.gov APIs
supports: SEC publishes a documentation page for the data.sec.gov APIs including the submissions API.
SEC describes API freshness in terms of dissemination ('as filings are disseminated'), not acceptance.
The page is silent on every field name, including acceptanceDateTime; it defines no JSON field schema at all.
SEC does label times elsewhere on the same page ('approximately 3:00 a.m. ET'), so the absence of a timezone for submission timestamps is not a lack of vocabulary.
does_not_support: It does NOT define acceptanceDateTime, its format, or its timezone.
It does NOT state that any submission-API timestamp is UTC.
It does NOT describe how any date/time field is serialised.

quotes.text: The JSON structures are updated throughout the day, in real time, as submissions are disseminated.
quotes.supports: API freshness is described relative to dissemination

quotes.text: In addition, a bulk ZIP file is available to download all the JSON structures for an API. This ZIP file is updated and republished nightly at approximately 3:00 a.m. ET.
quotes.supports: SEC does use an explicit ET label when it wants one

quotes.text: The APIs are updated in real-time as filings are disseminated. The submissions API is updated with a typical processing delay of less than a second; the xbrl APIs are updated with a typical processing delay of under a minute. However these processing delays may be longer during peak filing times.
quotes.supports: submissions API updated in real-time as filings are disseminated

title: Webmaster Frequently Asked Questions - SEC, Last Reviewed or Updated: Aug. 23, 2024
source_kind: SEC staff FAQ (informal support page, not a technical specification)
supports: This FAQ is the ONLY SEC web page located that names the ACCEPTANCE-DATETIME header, defines Acceptance Date / Acceptance Time, and states a timezone for acceptance time: EST.
It defines FILED AS OF DATE and contrasts it with the acceptance timestamps.
It states explicitly that no timestamp exists for when filing content first becomes available on sec.gov.
It quantifies the acceptance-to-availability lag (often within 1-3 minutes) and disclaims any guarantee.
It points readers to the PDS Technical Specification for header tag definitions - a pointer that does not actually hold for ACCEPTANCE-DATETIME (see S10).
does_not_support: It does NOT cover acceptanceDateTime in the data.sec.gov JSON API.
Its EST label is not DST-aware on its face (it says EST, not Eastern time) and it never mentions daylight saving time.
It is an FAQ, not a normative specification, and carries no effective-date semantics beyond Last Reviewed or Updated.

title: Accessing EDGAR Data - SEC, Last Reviewed or Updated: June 26, 2024
source_kind: SEC operational documentation for EDGAR data access
supports: Documents EDGAR's daily operating window (6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. ET) and the nightly index build starting about 10:00 p.m. ET.
Documents the 5:30 p.m. ET submission cut-off and that affected filings are disseminated the NEXT business day and appear in the following business day's index.
Documents that the index files carry only a date filed field - no time of day.
Documents that post-acceptance corrections are folded into index builds and that full/quarterly indexes are rebuilt weekly (so indexes are not immutable).
Points to the PDS Technical Specification for SGML header structure.
does_not_support: It gives no timezone for any acceptance timestamp.
It publishes no per-filing public-availability time.

quotes.text: EDGAR accepts new filer applications, new filings, and changes to filer data each business day, Monday through Friday, from 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m., ET. Indexes incorporating the current business day's filings are updated nightly starting about 10:00 p.m., ET; the process is usually completed within a few hours. Some filing submissions that begin after 5:30 p.m. ET—or 10:00 p.m. for Ownership forms 3, 4, 5—will be disseminated the next business day, showing up in the following business day's index.
quotes.supports: operating window, nightly index build, 5:30 p.m. ET / next-business-day dissemination rule

quotes.text: Filings are sometimes authorized by SEC staff for removal or correction for a variety of reasons at the filer's request including, but not limited to, the document was submitted for the wrong filer, the document was a duplicate of a previously filed document, the document in its current form was unreadable, or the document contained sensitive information. Corrections processed during a given business day will be incorporated in the indexes built that evening. However, removals processed on subsequent business days will not be reflected in any previous daily, feed, or oldload index. The full and quarterly index files are rebuilt weekly, early on Saturday mornings, so that any post-acceptance correction (PAC) deletes or updates are incorporated.
quotes.supports: PAC handling and index rebuild cadence

source_kind: the normative filer-facing manual for EDGAR filing
supports: Defines what EDGAR acceptance means operationally: the filing passed EDGAR's processing rules and, if live, will be disseminated.

quotes.text: and detailed error messages. EDGAR will either accept or suspend your filing. Acceptance means that the filing meets all of the EDGAR processing rules and, if live, the filing will be disseminated. Suspended means that the filing contains serious errors that you must correct. You can correct the errors and resubmit the filing. A suspended filing will not be disseminated nor will fees be deducted from your account.

quotes.text: When the EDGAR system has completed the processing of your submission, if it is live and public, it will be transmitted electronically to a number of third parties. (Certain non-public documents will not be immediately disseminated but may be subsequently disseminated if they meet certain criteria.) Dissemination can often occur within seconds of your transmission. Private companies may post your filing on their websites for public use of their subscribers. The filings are also posted on SEC.gov.

title: 17 CFR 232.13 - Date of filing; adjustment of filing date (Regulation S-T Rule 13); GPO/govinfo CFR compilation dated 2025-04-01
source_kind: federal regulation (legally operative text)
supports: The legally operative rule is the business day on which a filing is received by the Commission (receipt-based), subject to conditions.
The 5:30 p.m. cut-off is defined in terms of Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect - the regulation is explicitly DST-aware.
Special later cut-offs (10 p.m.) exist for Rule 462(b) registrations and for forms 3/4/5, 144, 13D/13G, 14N.
The rule time-stamps the moment a direct transmission commences, not the moment EDGAR finishes accepting.
does_not_support: It does not mention EDGAR's ACCEPTANCE-DATETIME field or any data format.
It does not define a public-dissemination timestamp.

quotes.text: (1) Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, the business day on which a filing is received by the Commission shall be the date of filing thereof, if:
quotes.supports: filing date = business day of receipt, subject to conditions

quotes.text: (2) If the conditions of paragraph (a)(1) of this section are otherwise satisfied, all filings submitted by direct transmission commencing on or before 5:30 p.m. Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect, shall be deemed filed on the same business day, and all filings submitted by direct transmission commencing after 5:30 p.m. Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect, shall be deemed filed as of the next business day.
quotes.supports: THE decisive legal statement: 5:30 p.m. Eastern Standard/Daylight time, DST-aware, next business day otherwise

quotes.text: (4) Notwithstanding paragraph (a)(2) of this section, a Form 3, 4, or 5 (referenced in §§ 249.103, 249.104, and 249.105 of this chapter, respectively), a Schedule 14N (referenced in § 240.14n-101 of this chapter), a Form 144 (referenced in § 239.144 of this chapter), or a Schedule 13D or Schedule 13G, inclusive of any amendments thereto (§§ 240.13d-101 and 240.13d-102 of this chapter), submitted by direct transmission commencing on or before 10 p.m. Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Time, whichever is currently in effect, shall be deemed filed on the same business day.

title: EDGAR Public Dissemination Service (PDS) System - SEC, Last Reviewed or Updated: Aug. 1, 2025
source_kind: SEC page describing the paid dissemination feed
supports: PDS exists to give the public an accurate, complete and fast method of obtaining all accepted and valid EDGAR filings; transmission is as soon as reasonably feasible after receipt by PDS.
SEC states the system was changed specifically to ensure SEC.gov availability precedes PDS availability - so PDS delivery is not even the first public moment.
This is the closest SEC comes to a public-dissemination definition, and it deliberately avoids promising a per-filing dissemination time.
does_not_support: No per-filing dissemination timestamp is published or promised.

quotes.text: The EDGAR Public Dissemination Service (PDS) System became operational on November 1, 1998, to provide the public an accurate, complete and fast method of obtaining all accepted and valid EDGAR filings. This privatized PDS System is managed by Maximus Federal Consulting, LLC and is the primary source to receive a dedicated feed of all public EDGAR filings. Subscribers are required to enter into a paid Subscription Agreement with Maximus Federal Consulting, LLC to access this service.
quotes.supports: PDS purpose and paid-subscription nature

quotes.text: Transmission by Internet connection of all public filings acquired and accepted by EDGAR as soon as reasonably feasible following receipt of filing data by the PDS.
quotes.supports: as soon as reasonably feasible - explicitly not a fixed timestamp

quotes.text: The EDGAR PDS New Subscriber Document (updated 08/01/2025) provides configuration, testing, maintenance, and billing information to potential and existing subscribers of the EDGAR public dissemination service feed. This document was updated to reflect modifications to the EDGAR system to ensure that EDGAR filings are available to the public on the SEC website before such filings are made available to the public dissemination system (PDS).
quotes.locator: section: EDGAR PDS New Subscriber Document
quotes.supports: SEC.gov availability is engineered to precede PDS availability

title: Raw SGML header (.hdr.sgml) for accession 0000064670-15-000002 (Medtronic 8-K)
source_kind: SEC-published data artifact - the exact header block in question 4
supports: The header contains ACCEPTANCE-DATETIME 20150217071853 with no timezone marker, no offset and no suffix.
It also contains FILING-DATE 20150217 and PUBLIC-DOCUMENT-COUNT 3, matching the field names in S4 and S10.
There is no TIMEZONE, UTC-OFFSET or equivalent element anywhere in the header.
does_not_support: The header itself documents nothing about its own timezone.

title: data.sec.gov submissions API payload for CIK 0000064670 (SEC-published artifact)
source_kind: SEC-published data artifact - the exact API the study uses
supports: The submissions JSON serialises acceptance as acceptanceDateTime with a literal Z suffix and millisecond precision, e.g. 2015-02-17T12:18:53.000Z.
For this CIK all 1001 rows in filings.recent use the same ...000Z shape; no row carries a numeric offset such as -05:00.
The JSON exposes filingDate separately (date-only), mirroring the .txt FILED AS OF DATE field.
does_not_support: Nothing in the payload or in SEC documentation says what the Z means or how the value was derived (see S1).

quotes.supports: the Z-suffixed serialisation for the same filing whose header reads 20150217071853
